faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: How do I change the font size of text when I print from software in Windows?
faqs.answer: You need to select the text or font size in the software you are printing from, not the printer driver. For detailed instructions, contact the company for the application you are printing from.

faqs.question: Where can I get replacement parts or a service manual?
faqs.answer: You can purchase replacement parts and service manuals from an Epson Authorized Customer Care Center or Epson parts distributor.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

faqs.question: Heavy coated or thick paper does not load correctly or loads skewed. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The paper you are using may be too heavy or glossy for the paper roller to pick up. Be sure the paper is within printer specifications.

faqs.question: Does OS X support manual duplex printing with my product?
faqs.answer: This feature is not supported in Mac OS X. However, if your printer has a built-in automatic duplexer, auto-duplexing is supported in Mac OS X 10.6 (Snow Leopard).

faqs.question: Calibration doesn't seem to have any effect. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure that whenever you turn off the printer, you are always using the printer's power button. Never use an external switch, such as a power strip, surge protector, or power protector, to turn off the printer. If you turn the printer off using an external switch, calibration settings will not be saved.

faqs.question: Are the ink cartridges refillable?
faqs.answer: EPSON does not recommend refilling ink cartridges. Refilled cartridges can cause print quality problems. In the printer's User's Guide, we advise "Use only genuine EPSON ink cartridges and do not refill them. Other products may cause damage not covered by EPSON's warranty".

faqs.question: The ink cartridge latch broke. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The common mistake that the Stylus Color IIs owners make is lifting the gray lid while the print head is on the outside of the printer which can cause a plastic piece to break. The print heads should work just fine even without that piece that broke off or came loose. All that spring loaded, plastic piece is for is to prevent you from accidentally removing the ink cartridge when the print head is outside of the printer (which you never want to do). The printhead on this printer should only be taken out when it switching between the color and black cartridge. If you are changing an old cartridge for a new cartridge, you have to make sure that the blue clamp is not opened and the head stays in the printer. For example, if you were changing the black cartridge on your printer, you would follow the instructions listed below:
Start with the problem printhead installed into the printer, then follow these steps.
Please follow this procedure to clear the flashing error light:
Factory Reset:
1) Shut printer off.
2) Hold down the Alt and Pause buttons while powering on the printer (continue holding for approx. 5 seconds and release).
3) The Error light should be on solid.
4) Hold down the Load/Eject until the Pause and Economy start to blink.
5) Release Load/Eject then press the Alt button to initialize the printer.
If the issue persists, please try the following to clear the light.
Reseating the Ink Cartridge:
1) Pause the printer
2) Press the Alt button until the print head starts to shift over (then release the Alt)
3) Lift the Gray Clamp that holds the ink cartridge all the way open then clamp it back down
*** MAKE SURE YOU DO NOT TAKE INK CARTRIDGE OUT ***
4) Once the clamp is closed, press and release the Alt button to recharge the Ink Delivery system (takes about 2 minutes).

faqs.question: Does OS X support manual duplex printing with my product?
faqs.answer: This feature is not supported in Mac OS X. However, if your printer has a built-in automatic duplexer, auto-duplexing is supported in Mac OS X 10.6 (Snow Leopard).

faqs.question: Why is the error light flashing after I changed the cartridge?
faqs.answer:
The situation you are encountering happens as a result of an ink cartridge being changed improperly. When you install a new ink cartridge the print head for that cartridge must be locked into the printer. You do not want to take out the print head, and then change the cartridge while the print head is in your hand. If you do the printer will show an error light on the control panel.
Start with the problem printhead installed into the printer, then follow these steps to clear the flashing error light.
Factory Reset:
1) Shut printer off.
2) Hold down the Alt and Pause buttons while powering on the printer (continue holding for approx. 5 seconds and release).
3) The Error light should be on solid.
4) Hold down the Load/Eject until the Pause and Economy start to blink.
5) Release Load/Eject then press the Pause button to initialize the printer.
If the issue persists, please try the following to clear the light.
Reseating the Ink Cartridge:
1) Pause the printer
2) Press the Alt button until the print head starts to shift over (then release the Alt)
3) Lift the Gray Clamp that holds the ink cartridge all the way open then clamp it back down
*** MAKE SURE YOU DO NOT TAKE INK CARTRIDGE OUT ***
4) Once the clamp is closed, press and release the Alt button to recharge the Ink Delivery system (takes about 2 minutes).
5) You may need to run a few cleaning cycles to help recharge the ink supply.

faqs.question: How do I install the ink cartridge?
faqs.answer: Use the inside front cover of the printer as a reference. Press pause, press and hold ALT for five seconds. Remove the yellow tape seal from the top of the ink cartridge and insert it into the printer. Press the locking clamp down firmly, you should hear a good solid click. Press the ALT button, when the pause light stops flashing the printer is ready. In either case, initial installation or replacement, snap the locking clamp down firmly to ensure the inner seal is broken. The Setup Guide pages 1-5 through 1-9 has a detailed step-by-step procedure including diagrams for installing the ink cartridges. If you continue to have difficulties after reading and following the procedure, call the EPSON Connection Technical Support group for further assistance.

faqs.question: I have just installed the ink cartridges and the ink out light flashes and the pause light stays on. How can I clear my product?
faqs.answer: Make sure the yellow tape is removed from the top of the cartridge and that the cartridge is correctly installed; follow the procedure for replacing the ink cartridge in the Reference Guide. Turn the printer off and back on. If the condition persists, follow the procedures for replacing the ink cartridges and lift the print head locking lever and snap it down firmly to ensure that you have broken the new seal. You should hear a good solid click. If you continue to have difficulties, the printer may need to go in for service. If the printer is within the dealers exchange period, have the printer exchanged.

faqs.question: My product is not producing any black ink and the error light keeps flashing. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Slow flashing indicates the ink level is low, fast flashing indicates the printer is out of ink. Using the inside front cover of the printer as a guide, perform a cleaning cycle (BLACK Cleaning) Press PAUSE button, then ALT and Pause. If the problem persists, replace the black ink cartridge and try printing again. If you continue to have problems, have the printer sent in for repair.

faqs.question: The print head assembly is not moving over so that I can install the ink cartridge. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Refer to the underside of the printer's front cover as a guide. Ensure that the cartridge installation procedure has been followed. Press the pause button and check to see if the light comes on. If the light does not come on, disconnect the printer cable and try it again. If the problem still persists, the printer may need to go in for service. If the printer is within the dealer's exchange period, have the printer exchanged.

faqs.question: Can I use sheet labels with my product?
faqs.answer: The printer is capable of printing sheet labels designed specifically for ink jet printers. To avoid paper jams, manually load sheet labels into the printer, one sheet at a time.

faqs.question: Heavy coated or thick paper does not load correctly or loads skewed. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The paper you are using may be too heavy or glossy for the paper roller to pick up. Be sure the paper is within printer specifications.

faqs.question: The output I am getting from my is unacceptable. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the economy light on the printer is not on, and if printing on Epson special coated paper, check to ensure that the you are printing on the coated side of the paper. If the Economy light is on, hold down the ALT button, and press Load/Eject until both Economy/Condensed lights are off. Economy mode is only intended for printing rough drafts and should not be enabled for normal print. Try printing again. If printing has not improved, perform a cleaning cycle (COLOR Cleaning) Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Print Mode, or (BLACK Cleaning) Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Pause. Print the demo page to see if printing has improved (Power on the printer while holding down the ALT button for 10 seconds; until data light comes on or paper loads). If the quality is acceptable, verify that the correct driver is selected as the default driver. Make sure that COLOR is selected in the driver. Ensure that HALFTONING is NOT selected in the driver. Manipulate the Stylus driver settings. You may also want to manipulate the settings within the application to achieve the optimum print results. If the quality from the demo page is not acceptable, check the type of paper being used. The EPSON special coated paper which is specifically made for the Stylus inkjet series printers, delivers the best printed output. If the problem persists, replace the ink cartridge. The trouble shooting guide located in chapter six of the Users Manual provides additional information. If the print quality is still unacceptable, have the printer sent in for repair.

faqs.question: My print looks wavy or stair steps. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Print the demo page to ensure the printer is operating properly. If the print is normal, try moving the printer to another computer to eliminate the possibility of a defective printer cable, parallel port or software problem. If the problem persists, try recalibrating the printer with the Calibrat.exe utility program. Try printing again. If the problem persists, the printer may need to go in for service.

faqs.question: My printout is blurry or smeared. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Try cleaning the plastic output guide inside the printer with a soft dry cloth. If the problem persists, take the printer to an Epson Authorized Service Center.

faqs.question: I am not getting either black or color on the demo page. What should I do?
faqs.answer: If this is a new installation or if the cartridges have been recently replaced, follow the procedure for replacing the ink cartridges and try lifting the print head locking lever and snapping it down firmly to ensure that you have broken the cartridge seal. You should hear a good solid click. Try running the demo page again. Perform two cleaning cycles; (COLOR Cleaning) Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Pause, or (BLACK Cleaning) Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Pause. If this does not correct the problem, the printer may need to go in for service. If the printer is within the dealers exchange period, have the printer exchanged.

faqs.question: One of my colors is missing. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Calibrate colors in the driver setup to the specific application or image. Set to Default and adjust from there. If the color is still missing perform selftest (Press Load/Eject and power printer on) and check that seven colors are produced. If seven colors are not produced, print default settings (Press Economy/Condensed and power printer on) to inspect dots. If test print shows missing dots, perform two cleaning cycles; (COLOR Cleaning) Press the PAUSE Button, then, Alt and Pause 'OR' (BLACK Cleaning) Press the PAUSE then, Alt and Pause. Run the selftest again to see if printing has improved (Power on the Printer while holding down the Load/Eject Button. If the selftest shows no dots of one of the four colors, try replacing the ink cartridge. If the condition persists, have the printer sent in for repair.

faqs.question: My text looks dark gray. How can I get my product to print my text a truer black?
faqs.answer: First, make sure the black cartridge is installed and the economy light on the printer is not on. This will ensure that the economy mode option is not selected. Perform a black cleaning cycle; (BLACK Cleaning) Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Pause. Run the print demo to see if printing has improved (Power on the Printer while holding down the ALT-Button). If this does not correct the problem, replace the black ink cartridge. If the black text on the demonstration page is acceptable, the problem may be a setting in the printer driver. The monochrome setting in the driver will produce a truer black than the color setting. Enabling "microweave" and "disabling ink density correction" within the Stylus COLOR IIs printer will also give a darker truer black output.

faqs.question: My printout has lines running through it. What should I do?
faqs.answer: This is called banding and may be caused by a clogged nozzle. Print the demo page by pressing the ALT button while applying power to the printer. Check to see if white lines appear through your text. If the white lines are present, perform two cleaning cycles; (COLOR Cleaning) Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Pause, or (BLACK Cleaning) Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Pause. If the cleaning cycles do not correct the problem, perform default settings (Press the Pause button and power the printer on) to ensure that "Autoline Feed" is off. If the condition persists, have the printer sent in for service. The trouble shooting guide located in chapter six of the Users Manual provides additional information.

faqs.question: My printout is missing some characters. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Video driver conflict
Some video drivers may cause a conflict in memory between the printerdriver and video memory. Try changing to the Windows video driver provided by Microsoft or check to see if the video card manufacturer has an updated video driver available. This is often the cause of strange printing problems such as heavy banding and missing characters.

faqs.question: My product's control panel locks up after I print a document from Windows. The buttons on the panel do not respond unless I disconnect the parallel cable from the back of my product. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Some computers send an initialize/reset signal during the boot-up process. If the printer cable picks up any noise during this process, the initialize line will not complete its reset phase and cause the control panel to lock. Try booting the computer to Windows, then turn the printer ON using the printer's power switch and try printing again. A defective cable can also cause this situation. Make sure you are using a fully-shielded parallel cable, preferably 6 feet or less.

faqs.question: My product is severely malfunctioning (no power, loud noises). What should I do?
faqs.answer: Remove the printer cable from the printer and verify the power source. Make sure that all packing material has been removed (head lock transportation key, etc.). Power the printer off and back on and perform the reset function on the printer. If the problem persists, take the printer to an Epson Authorized Service Center.
